findings.title: Migration raises NoMethodError when no `embed_category` setting row matches
findings.body: The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. `embed_category` is a non-default, rarely-set setting, so on virtually every existing site (and on every fresh install, where the `site_settings` row does not exist at all) the query returns zero rows, `[0]` is `nil`, and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`. This aborts `rake db:migrate` and blocks deploys/installs entirely. The result must be checked for emptiness (e.g. `rows = execute(...); category_id = rows.first ? rows.first['id'].to_i : 0`).

findings.title: Fallback category lookup also dereferences a possibly-empty result set
findings.body: `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i` assumes a row always exists. `uncategorized_category_id` is a hidden setting with a default of `-1`; if it was never persisted to the `site_settings` table (the default is only in YAML), `[0]` is `nil` and the migration crashes with `NoMethodError`. Guard the result, and fall back to a sane value.

findings.title: Migrated host values are not normalized (and not SQL-escaped), breaking embedding after upgrade
findings.body: Hosts are copied verbatim from the old `embeddable_hosts` setting via raw `INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. The old setting legitimately contained values like `http://example.com` or `https://example.com/1234` (see the removed specs in `spec/models/site_setting_spec.rb`), but `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` matches with `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, i.e. bare hostnames only. Because the raw INSERT bypasses the model's `before_validation` scheme/path stripping, rows such as `http://example.com` will never match a referer and embedding silently stops working for those sites after the upgrade. Values should be normalized (strip scheme/path, strip whitespace/CR) before insert. Additionally, interpolating `h` directly into SQL without quoting will produce a syntax error (or injection) if a host value contains a quote; use `quote()` / a prepared statement.

findings.title: `create_table ... force: true` can drop an existing table and the migration is irreversible
findings.body: `force: true` issues a `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS embeddable_hosts` before creating it, so re-running the migration (or running it on a database where the table already exists) silently destroys all existing embeddable host rows. In addition, the migration is declared with `change` but contains `execute` statements (including `DELETE FROM site_settings`), which cannot be reversed, so `db:rollback` will fail. Drop `force: true` and implement explicit `up`/`down`.

findings.title: `before_validation` raises NoMethodError when host is nil; no presence validation
findings.body: `self.host.sub!(...)` is called unconditionally in `before_validation`. If `host` is `nil` (e.g. `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?`, or `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigning `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` when the key is absent) this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil`, producing a 500 instead of a validation error — and the DB column is `null: false`. Add `validates_presence_of :host` and guard the callback (`return if host.blank?`). Note also that `sub!` mutates the assigned string in place, so it mutates the caller's/params' string object; using non-destructive `sub` is safer.

findings.title: update/destroy crash with 500 when the id does not exist
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns `nil` for an unknown or already-deleted id; `update` then calls `save_host(nil)` and `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`, both raising `NoMethodError` and returning a 500. This is reachable from the admin UI whenever two admins edit concurrently or a stale page is used. Use `find_by` plus `raise Discourse::NotFound` (or `render_json_error`) when the record is missing.

findings.title: Parsed referer host is not downcased before the case-insensitive comparison
findings.body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the stored column but not the value extracted from the URL. `URI('http://EvilTrout.com').host` returns `EvilTrout.com`, so any referer or embed URL containing an upper-case hostname fails the match and embedding/topic retrieval is rejected even though the host is registered. Use `host.downcase` in the query.

findings.title: No uniqueness validation or index on host
findings.body: Nothing prevents two `EmbeddableHost` rows for the same host (the admin UI makes this trivial). `record_for_host` returns `.first` of an unordered query, so which category an imported topic lands in becomes non-deterministic for duplicated hosts. Add `validates_uniqueness_of :host` (case-insensitive) and a unique index in the migration.

findings.title: `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` is a no-op that reports success
findings.body: `update` only re-renders the freshly fetched `@embedding` OpenStruct; it never reads or persists any params. The client's `admin-embedding` controller `saveChanges()` calls `embedding.update({})` against this endpoint, so a user clicking save would get a success response with nothing saved. (The embedding template also has no save button, so `saveChanges` is currently dead code.) Either implement the update or remove the route/action and the unused client action.

findings.title: Plural embedded hydration discards ids even when the lookup fails
findings.body: In the new `_ids` branch, `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` is followed by an unconditional `delete obj[k]`. `hydrated` is always a truthy array, so `|| []` is dead, and when `_lookupSubType` cannot resolve an id (no side-loaded collection in the payload for that type) the resulting array contains `undefined` entries while the original `*_ids` attribute is deleted. Callers then iterate a collection of `undefined` with no way to recover the ids. The singular branch correctly only deletes when hydration succeeded; the plural branch should likewise filter out unresolved ids and keep the raw ids when nothing could be hydrated.

findings.title: `String.replace('_','-')` only replaces the first underscore
findings.body: `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace('_', '-'))` uses a string (not regex/global) argument, so only the first underscore is converted. Any admin model type with more than one underscore (e.g. `some_embeddable_host`) will not be matched and will be requested from `/` instead of `/admin/`, yielding a 404/403. Use `type.replace(/_/g, '-')`.

findings.title: Fabricator definitions were swapped between files
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`). This is clearly an accidental swap: the file names no longer describe their contents, which breaks Fabrication's `<name>_fabricator.rb` naming convention and makes the definitions impossible to locate by name. Move each definition into the correspondingly named file.

findings.title: New admin endpoints have no behavioural tests
findings.body: Both new controller specs only assert `Controller < Admin::AdminController`. There is no coverage for `create`/`update`/`destroy` of embeddable hosts (success, validation failure, missing id — which currently 500s, see `embeddable_hosts_controller.rb`), for the default-to-uncategorized behaviour, or for the `embedding#show`/`#update` payload shape that the new Ember store/serializer rely on. Given that this PR changes who can embed the forum (a security-relevant allow-list), at least request-level specs for create/update/destroy and non-admin access should be added.

findings.title: `expandable_first_post?` spec no longer tests what its description says
findings.body: `Topic#expandable_first_post?` was changed to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` and no longer consults embeddable hosts at all, yet the spec still has `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` (which now only passes because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is false) and a `describe 'with an emeddable host'` block whose `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` has no effect on the method under test. The descriptions are misleading (and contain a typo, "emeddable"); either drop the host references or restore a real host dependency.
